existing_issues.issue: Level too low. The RCM 2021 syllabus lets only Levels 9-10 use the Flesch patterns, IMSLP calls the book 'the advanced violinist's scale bible', and Polish authors (Umińska, Cofalik) build their advanced scale books on it. Title and category are right; the catalogue's Level 3 anchor should move to about Level 5.

Title omits the descriptor that its companion Op. 63 carries: Op. 64 is the set of six études for left-hand technique (Wikipedia work list; the Hamelle edition issued Opp. 63 and 64 as Cahiers 1 and 2, plate J. 4324 H). The BnF record titles both cahiers 'pour développer la technique de l'archet', so the descriptor is worth a second check.
Published in two parts (Part 1: The Left Hand; Part 2: The Bow). Under the one-entry-per-part rule it could be split; the single entry and Level 8 are otherwise fine.
existing_issues.suggested_title: The Artist's Technique of Violin Playing, Op. 12 Part 1 (The Left Hand) and Part 2 (The Bow)

Korguev (Korguyev), Sergei - 'Double-Stop Exercises' (PWM print-on-demand, 32 pp.); Russian group
Fortunatov, Konstantin - 'Studies in the Changes of Positions' (PWM Cat. 1385, used in Polish schools); Russian group
Kotek, Iosif (Józef) - '6 Practical Studies, Op. 8' (IMSLP; PWM ed. Umińska); Russian/Polish, not covered here

Venzl, Josef - 'Universal Studies, Op. 88' and 'Schule des Lagenspiels, Op. 78' (Oertel, Hannover); nationality unclear, check German group

note: Method: IMSLP author pages and wikitext for Czech, Hungarian, Polish, Austrian and Balkan authors; then Czech National Library (NKP), BnF, PWM catalogue pages, Polish Music Library, Wikipedia and retailer listings for works not on IMSLP. 4 of the allotted WebSearches were used. Existing rows touched and verified: ids 619, 624, 667, 668, 2111, 2112, 2508, 2509, 3248 (see existing_issues). Findings that contradict the task text: 'Fingerboard Geography' is by Barbara Barber (Alfred), not Ondříček; 'Basic Studies' is Flesch's Urstudien; the Ondříček books are the Peters/Nickau 'Meistertechnik' set with Siegfried Mittelmann (IMSLP calls Mittelmann an alias of Dounis, the Czech National Library names him as a separate person, unresolved). No own technical books were found for Kocian (beginner school only), Karel Hoffmann, Jan Mařák, Jan Kubelík (only editions of others or concertos), Barcewicz, Kochański or Totenberg, and none for Sándor Végh or Géza Szilvay beyond the scale books listed. Levels are mostly estimates: the only syllabus evidence found was the RCM 2021 resource list and Level 9-10 scale rule (Hřímalý, Flesch, Dounis, Wieniawski, Nováček) and a Kraków primary-school literature list for the Polish scale books; level_basis says 'estimate' wherever nothing better exists. Likely overlaps with other researchers (decide at merge): Dounis (Greek-American; 17 entries here), Halir, Singer, Hellmesberger Jr., Kneisel, and Flesch's Etüden-Sammlung (an anthology of other composers' études, kept because it has a study purpose). Gaps: Bulgarian, Romanian, Serbian, Croatian and Slovenian national-library catalogues were not searched; Slovak National Library, OSZK and the full EMB catalogue were only sampled; Polish National Library not searched. Bloch's Tonleiterschule opus number (Op. 5) rests on one retailer listing and is left out of the title; Heller's nationality could not be verified. Granularity: Lipiński Op. 27 and Kątski Op. 16 are one entry each although published in several issues; Hellmesberger Op. 220 and Cofalik's Scales (five parts in one volume) are single entries because per-part content or separate publication could not be shown.
